rules.title: Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords in Los Angeles cannot end a tenancy without a legally listed just cause, and if the eviction is a no-fault eviction (not the tenant's fault), the landlord must pay the tenant relocation assistance. The ordinance applies once a tenant has lived in the unit for at least six months or their original lease has expired.
rules.coverage_conditions: Covers most residential rental properties in the City of Los Angeles that are not already regulated by the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO); can apply to buildings built after October 1, 1978 and even to single-family dwellings.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate situations, cooperatives under certain circumstances, some non-profit homeless facilities or short-term substance abuse treatment centers, and some properties owned by HACLA or the government.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the unit is already regulated by the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO), and whether the tenant has lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease has expired

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482)
rules.requirement: For covered rental units in buildings older than 15 years, annual rent increases are capped at 5% plus the regional change in cost of living, or 10%, whichever is lower.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental properties in buildings older than 15 years (rolling basis) that are not otherwise exempt, unless the unit is already covered by a local rent stabilization ordinance such as the City's RSO.
rules.exemptions: Units constructed within the last 15 years (rolling basis); units deed-restricted as low/moderate-income affordable housing; certain dormitories; two-unit properties where the owner occupied the second unit for the entire tenancy; single-family homes/condominiums meeting ownership and written-notice conditions; units already subject to the City's RSO.
rules.quoted_span: (Annual rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region in which the property is located, or 10% whichever is lower).

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the unit is deed-restricted/regulated affordable housing, whether a two-unit property's second unit was owner-occupied for the full tenancy, whether a single-family home/condo owner is a natural person (not a corporation/LLC/REIT) who gave the required written notice, and whether the unit is already subject to the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO)

rules.conflict_note: Text states two different applicable percentages for different periods (8.8% for Aug 2023-Jul 2024 and 8.9% for Aug 2024-Jul 2025); these are annually adjusted figures under the same statutory formula, not changes to the law itself, and no single statutory effective date is given in this chunk.
